observations: The population grew steadily, from about 276 organisms early on to 2,400 by the end.
Life was cheap and fast: 22,864 organisms were born and 20,464 died, averaging 704 ticks each — about 16 lifetimes over the run.
19,952 of 22,864 births were offspring rather than fresh spawns, reaching generation 21, and one organism had 26 children.
The largest surviving lineage held 963 of 2,400 organisms, across 17 lineages in all.
Organisms joined up: the largest compound reached order 19 and held for 10 ticks, though none lasted long enough to count as stable.
Of the 3,388,464 energy that ever existed here — 408,000 to begin with and 2,980,464 arriving since — 87% was burned and 13% was still held at the end.
Food piled up uneaten, sitting near its cap of 4,800 by the end — nothing was hungry enough to clear it.
The motion clamp bit on 43.6% of steps — this world is hot enough that the guardrail, not the chemistry, was setting how far things moved. Lower the temperature or add sub-steps.
